title: The ten per cent
text: {{1}} is not easy being left-handed in a right-handed world: scissors, spiral notebooks and lecture-hall desks have all been designed {{2}} the right hand, and a tin opener simply sulks {{3}} you hold it the wrong way up. {{4}} was long a belief that left-handers died younger, a myth built {{5}} a misread study of old tombstones. In reality, left-handers, {{6}} brains must constantly adapt to right-handed tools, often develop stronger two-handed coordination, and in interactive sports they beat right-handers {{7}} often than chance would predict, {{8}} opponents rarely meet anyone like them.

gaps.hint: dummy subject: ___ is not easy being left-handed
gaps.explanation: 'It is not easy being…' — the comment structure.

gaps.hint: time word: sulks ___ you hold it wrongly
gaps.explanation: The refusal happens when the holding happens: when.

gaps.hint: pronoun: ___ was long a belief that
gaps.explanation: The existential clause: there was a belief.

gaps.hint: preposition: a myth built ___ a study

gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the left-handers to their brains.

gaps.hint: adverb: beat right-handers ___ often than chance

gaps.explanation: The reason clause after the comma: because.
